attribution.note: Marcus directly endorses the causal explanation; the tentative example is also his.

semantics.note: The normalisation broadens wholesale factual fabrication to LLM hallucinations generally. The contract restores the narrower scope. The general causal assertion is firm; only the proposed explanation of the chicken example is tentative.

contract.note: Reading recombination as combining learned textual associations fairly respects the explicit analogy. Limiting assessment to wholesale factual fabrication is appropriate. The mechanism remains interpretive because Marcus does not specify its technical meaning.

evidence.note: Timely primary research relevant to association-based explanations, but its later systems and attribution results do not establish the required causal coverage for the fabrications at issue.
Timely research identifying training-data contributions in conversational models. This supplies an alternative contributing explanation without establishing that recombination is materially wrong.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's fair, narrower interpretation, neither item settles the causal claim. The packet lacks a trace of the illustrative fabrication and sufficiently broad controlled evidence for the proposed mechanism. Training-data effects do not independently refute it.
